author: @superm1

evidence.api_compatibility: Breaking change — version format shifted from X.Y.Z (e.g., 11.9.0) to YYYY.WW.N or YYYY.WW.0~<count>.<hash>. CMakeLists.txt now requires find_package(Python3) and runs tools/version.py at configure time, adding a hard Python3 dependency to the build. Dockerfile adds python3 to apt dependencies. contrib/debian/control adds python3 to Build-Depends. src/cpp/installer/Product.wxs.in now uses @LEMONADE_MSI_VERSION@ (derived from the date-part of the year) instead of @PROJECT_VERSION@. src/cpp/server/lemonade.manifest.in uses @LEMONADE_NUMERIC_VERSION@ instead of @PROJECT_VERSION@. The author acknowledged breaking changes and coordinated with other PRs (e.g., #3529) for release-time changes.
evidence.documentation: Module docstrings added to all three Python tools with usage examples. Inline CI comments updated (e.g., 'auto-generated from CMakeLists.txt' → 'auto-generated at configure time', 'Extract version' → 'Calculate version'). The PR references RFC discussion #3522. No external release notes or changelog entries are visible in the PR or repository at this time — the breaking version format change and new Python3 build dependency should be included in release notes when released.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No human has exercised the new source-tarball CI job on a release branch or tag. The new tools (tools/version.py, tools/source_archive.py, tools/release.py) have unit tests but have not been run end-to-end in a release-like scenario. The version stamping added to Docker build workflows has not been verified on an actual release build. The version non-determinism for main/bleeding-edge builds (same commit producing different versions on different dates) was raised during review and intentionally retained — this should be noted for the release notes.
evidence.review: Substantive review by @jeremyfowers (CI expertise per docs/dev/contribute.md) with 12 inline comments across .github/actions, .github/workflows, CMakeLists.txt, tools/version.py, tools/source_archive.py, and tools/release.py. All comments addressed before approval. First and latest approval both at 2026-09-14T17:54:50Z with no post-approval commits (the last three commits — 3f32c259, cc0eaf8c, b7e5373f — were all made on 2026-09-14 between 16:01–16:40, before the 17:54 approval). The reviewer correctly identified the need for `fetch-depth: 0` in the cpp-unit-tests checkout, requested module docstrings, flagged that main-branch versions are non-deterministic (time-based rather than commit-date-based), and suggested a deterministic release-helper script. The author addressed all concerns; the deterministic release helper (tools/release.py) was implemented in response to that review suggestion.
evidence.security: No concerns. tools/version.py, tools/source_archive.py, and tools/release.py only read git state and create local artifacts. No network calls, credential handling, code execution, or permission broadening introduced.
evidence.tests: Three new test files: test_version.py (101 lines, 12 tests covering .version override, release branch counting, existing tag continuity, exact release tag in detached checkout, and GITHUB_REF env support), test_source_archive.py (82 lines, 3 tests covering version stamp correctness, existing .version replacement, and default version helper usage), and test_release.py (124 lines, 7 tests covering branch selection by year/week, explicit hotfix branch selection, dry-run safety, actual tag creation and push, and existing-tag rejection). The docs_and_style workflow ran `python -m unittest test.test_version test.test_source_archive -v` and passed. Note: test_release.py is not in the docs_and_style trigger; it would run only if explicitly invoked.

maintainer_todos.text: Run `lemonade-server --version` or check the server startup log and confirm the version is in the new YYYY.WW.N format (e.g., `2026.39.0`) rather than the old X.Y.Z format (e.g., `11.9.0`).

subject: Implement new version handling scheme (#3539)
summary: Implements a new version handling scheme replacing CMakeLists.txt static versioning with a dynamic Python-based system that derives versions from git branches, tags, and timestamps.
verdict_reason: Major release infrastructure change with a breaking version format and new Python3 build dependency that has not been exercised in an end-to-end release scenario by a human.
